solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Manage somehow to produce and act at the same time

parts.note: to produce something is to make it
to act is to do something

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stage a production and perform in it simultaneously.
explanation.definitionFit: To make do is an idiom for coping with whatever resources happen to be available.

clue.text: Fruit gives chap vitality

parts.note: a chap is a man
go means energy or vitality, as in 'full of go'

explanation.surface: Eating fruit is said to give a fellow energy.
explanation.definitionFit: This tropical stone fruit is a common example of fruit.

clue.text: One joining in needlework

parts.note: it reads like a seamstress joining fabric, but it describes someone who links loops of yarn with needles

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who makes woollens on needles joins stitches together in a form of needlework.

clue.text: One of the odder army varieties of transport

indicators.note: varieties suggests these letters can be arranged in other forms

explanation.surface: Among the oddest kinds of military transport is a certain beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One of the' and 'of' are link words; the letters of ODDER ARMY rearrange, signalled by 'varieties'.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-humped camel has long carried goods and people across deserts, a form of transport.

clue.text: Prey of little boys

parts.note: Vic is a short form of the boy's name Victor
Tim is a short form of the boy's name Timothy

explanation.surface: Young lads are portrayed as falling prey to something.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who falls prey to another is a sufferer of attack, a synonym in noun sense.

clue.text: Risk having a dog at home

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Keeping a dog in the house is said to carry a danger.
explanation.definitionFit: To risk a penalty is to bring it upon oneself, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: Loudspeaker for one sending message?

definitions.meaning: a small high-frequency speaker unit in a sound system
someone who posts short messages on a social media platform

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a treble speaker and also a person posting on the platform formerly called Twitter.

clue.text: Where currency is equally divided

parts.note: currency suggests money, but it means a current of water, split evenly in the middle of a river

explanation.definitionFit: The centre of a river is the point equidistant from both banks, where the flow divides.

clue.text: Article on Rodin's mongrel dog

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: a mongrel is of mixed breed, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about a hybrid canine belonging to the sculptor Rodin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mongrel' turns RODIN into DIRON; 'dog' is the definition in its sense of a firedog, not an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A firedog is an iron support for logs in a fireplace, also called a dog.

clue.text: They smoothly finish off pieces of writing

definitions.meaning: levelled layers of cement or the strips used to level plaster and flooring

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both levelling layers of cement on a floor and lengthy written passages.

clue.text: Something much appreciated by card-players?

parts.note: the phrase means a lot, and for card-players a favourable hand dealt to them

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a great amount, and literally a favourable hand at cards.

clue.text: One operating still as a pirate

definitions.meaning: someone running an illicit still to distil liquor
someone making unauthorised copies of recordings or goods

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a smuggler or maker of illegal liquor and also a seller of pirated recordings.

clue.text: Child has a point to convey

parts.note: a tot is a small child
E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A youngster has a point he wants to get across.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry something from place to place is a meaning shared by both words.

clue.text: It's about time

parts.note: an exasperated phrase, read literally as a word meaning about, used before dates

explanation.definitionFit: This Latin word meaning approximately is placed before dates, so it is a word about time.

clue.text: One in the club has whip-round for cheese

indicators.note: has means the whip holds the club man within it
round says the whip goes around the other piece

parts.note: a cat-o'-nine-tails is a whip, shortened to cat
a member is someone belonging to a club

explanation.surface: A club member organises a collection of money to buy some cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft French cheese from Normandy, an example of cheese.

clue.text: Said to be celebrated

definitions.meaning: marked or kept, as with a holiday or festival

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both remarked and kept or marked, as a festival is.

clue.text: Counterpart of a Papal Bull that's above criticism?

definitions.text: Counterpart of a Papal Bull that's above criticism?

parts.words: Counterpart of a Papal Bull that's above criticism?
parts.note: a female bovine as the opposite of a bull, holy as a papal one, and an idea immune from criticism

explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for an idea or institution held to be beyond question, literally a holy cow.

clue.text: Used to be in a job

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both utilised and working for pay.

clue.text: He took in, in wild glee, what was left

definitions.text: He took in, in wild glee, what was left

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the other
wild suggests the letters are scattered out of order

parts.note: to eat is to take in food, past tense ate

explanation.surface: An heir gleefully pocketed whatever had been bequeathed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges the four letters of the clue's 'glee' into LEGE, and 'in' sets the eating verb inside after its third letter. Read whole, the clue also pictures an heir.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who receives a bequest takes in what was left in a will.

clue.text: Pack a quarter in of the very best

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: to cram is to pack tightly
E is east, one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stuff a fraction of the finest goods into a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: The best part of anything is called its finest portion, as the richest part rises to the top of milk.

clue.text: Cheer for most of the players at end of game

indicators.note: most of means the word loses its final two letters, keeping most of it

parts.note: a team in cricket or football has eleven players

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Applause greets most of the team at the close of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone up is to raise their spirits, a synonym in the verb sense.

clue.text: Sticks around, looking complacent

indicators.note: around means the word is turned the other way about

parts.note: to stick something is to glue or gum it

explanation.surface: Someone hangs about with an air of self-satisfaction.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-satisfied in appearance is the meaning of this adjective.

clue.text: Postwar conditions?

parts.note: suggests life after a war, but means the stipulations agreed to end one

explanation.definitionFit: The terms of a treaty ending a war are the conditions set for the peace that follows.

clue.text: Victoria, perhaps, when old and wrinkled?

definitions.text: Victoria, perhaps, when old and wrinkled?

parts.words: Victoria, perhaps, when old and wrinkled?
parts.note: Victoria seems a queen, but is a variety of plum, which dried becomes wrinkled

explanation.definitionFit: A dried plum, such as a Victoria plum, shrivels into this wrinkled fruit.

clue.text: Ridicules exams

definitions.meaning: practice examinations taken before the real ones, in British schools

explanation.definitionFit: The word means taunts and also trial examinations sat by British pupils before the real ones.

clue.text: Keeps quiet, like a sensible motorist does

definitions.meaning: a slang order to be silent

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is British slang for falling silent and also means fastening a seat belt.

clue.text: Slight wound is no handicap

definitions.meaning: a shallow mark on the skin
in golf a player with a handicap of zero

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a minor graze and also a golf term for a player with zero handicap.

clue.text: Almost the finest of ancient cities

definitions.note: a singular name; two ancient cities, in Egypt and Greece, bore it

indicators.note: almost means the phrase stops one letter short of the end

parts.note: the best means the finest

explanation.surface: A claim that one place was nearly the greatest city of the ancient world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link; the name belonged to two ancient cities, in Egypt and in Greece, which is why the definition is plural.
explanation.definitionFit: The name was borne by the Egyptian capital on the Nile and a leading Greek city-state.

clue.text: Ways to get round little children's demands

indicators.note: one piece is put around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: St is short for street, a way; two of them are STS
wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: Tips on how to sidestep what little ones keep asking for.
explanation.definitionFit: Children often clamour for confectionery, so candies are a typical demand of theirs.
